messages:
mike: Heads-up — we just hit another customer case where the gateway returns 502 instead of failing over to the next zone. This is for dedicated pools where the preferred region went unregistered after an AZ flap. We should add a region-cascade policy, not just immediate global fallback.

anya: I can repro locally with the dedicated test account. Agent didn't re-register for ~40s. Agree on cascade.

sam: Quick question: do we want header overrides (X-Region) + geo affinity + latency probes? My worry: sticky affinity can keep routing to a degraded pool if probes lag.

lin: Proposal sketch: policy order = 1) explicit header override (X-Region) 2) account-level pinned region group 3) geo-affinity within pinned region 4) latency-sensed fallthrough to next zone(s) 5) global fallback. Add TTL on any cached decision so we don't persist bad routing.

mike: Example pseudo rule (for discussion):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "policy": {
    "mode": "cascade",        // cascade | spillover | strict
    "priority": ["X-Region","account-pinned","geo","latency","global"],
    "cascade_order": ["us-west-2","us-west-1","us-east-1"],
    "probe": {"enabled": true, "timeout_ms": 200}
  }
}
```

routebot: deploy-bot: note: can add a synthetic probe to ensure pool healthy before routing.

anya: UX note — console should surface the full failover chain for each route and allow reorder via drag/drop. Also show expected latency/cost estimate per leg. Small animated preview would help platform->customer conversations.

sam: Also consider header precedence semantics. X-Region should be honored if present, but if target region is unhealthy should we respect a 'force' flag? e.g. `X-Region: us-west-2;force=true`

lin: Strong no for force by default. Force should be opt-in at account-level with audit logs and an allowlist. We can't let apps bypass SLOs silently.

mike: Telemetry: add fields to traces/span tags: selected_region, resolved_region_reason (header|pin|geo|probe), probe_latency_ms. Also increment a counter every time we trigger a failover and record which leg was chosen.

anya: Dashboard: add 'failover activations' graph last 24h and a table of recent route fallbacks with root cause. Also a per-route setting for pager thresholds (e.g. >5 failovers/min).

sam: Implementation note: route matcher flow should be deterministic: host/path match -> route policy resolution -> region selection. Header affects region selection only, not path matching.

lin: Agreed — keep the matcher separate. Also add a regression test that simulates AZ flaps and ensures we don't return 502 to the client (we should route to next healthy pool within 5s).

mike: Ops question: do we want a "spillover weight" vs strict cascade? e.g. preferred:100, second:20 so some traffic uses second pool proactively for capacity smoothing.

sam: Spillover is interesting — it's more like overflow/weighted fallback. Good for availability when you want gradual traffic shift.

anya: Console shorthand: show mode as 'strict' or 'spill' and a preview slider to simulate traffic distribution.

mike: I'll open a PR for the rule engine + add unit/integration tests. I'll draft a JSON policy schema and add to the spec. Ping me if you want to review.

lin: Please add a test for rapid re-register/unregister flapping. Also include metrics tags so on-call can filter by account/route.

sam: +1 for tests. Ping me on the PR.

routebot: created issue INF-4823: "region cascade policy + console UI" assigned to mike (https://ourjira/INF-4823)

mike: thanks all :thumbsup:
